Maria (CS): FYI escalation from Acme Labs — after last night's rollout some Spanish translation flows started returning English or truncated answers. Customer provided examples and says it was fine before rollout.
Suki (Support): Can you paste the exact prompts + API call they used? Also region, model param, and any request headers they set.
Maria (CS): Customer says they call our text-generation endpoint with model `rw-translate-medium-v2` and locale=es. Example prompt: 
````
Input (es): "¿Cuál es el mejor camino para llegar al centro desde el aeropuerto?"
Expected: Spanish answer with directions.
Got (post-rollout): "The best way is to take the A1..." (English) or sometimes just a 2-line snippet that looks cut off.
````
They attached curl repro: 
````bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rw-translate-medium-v2","input":"¿Cuál es el mejor camino para llegar al centro desde el aeropuerto?","metadata":{"locale":"es","customer_id":"acme-labs"}}'
````
They report p50 latency ~ 180ms normally, after rollout some requests jump to 700-1200ms and the output switches to English or returns a short snippet.
Ivan (Eng): deploy-bot shows the v2 routing rollout finished ~23:12 UTC last night. Possible routing rule mismatch where requests with locale header are routed to an English-only variant when capacity is low. Can you share the request ids and a few full request logs? Also any examples that include token-level response (so we can see if model started generating in English).
Maria (CS): Provided three request IDs and the customer log snippets. Pasting one snippet (sanitized):
````
request_id: r-20260316-01
model: rw-translate-medium-v2
route: eu-west-1 -> rw-translate-medium-v2@canary -> rw-translate-base-en@fallback
latencies: queue 12ms, start 195ms, first_token 720ms, total 895ms
response: 'The best way is to take the...'
````
Jacob (ML): That route chain stands out — fallback to `rw-translate-base-en` would explain English output. Two possibilities: (1) rollout policy allowed fallback to an en-only variant when canary couldn't serve (capacity/compatibility), (2) a model-compatibility tag got mis-set during the canary so the router thought en-only variant was compatible.
Suki (Support): Acme says this reproduces in eu-west and ap-south; they tried pinning `rw-translate-medium-v2:2026-03-15` in a test tenant and saw correct Spanish outputs still. So likely a routing/variant issue, not the model weights.
Ivan (Eng): I'll check routing logs + policy config for the v2 rollout. Quick check: can someone confirm if `fallback_policy` was set to `route_to_compatible` vs `reject` in the rollout? If it was permissive we should flip to `reject` temporarily for the translation family.
Jacob (ML): Also want tokenization traces: if tokenizer changed (lang-specific special tokens) in the v2 build, that can cause short/truncated outputs. But the fact pinning older version produces correct output points to routing. I'll run a quick local inference on the v2 binary with the same input and compare.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout rw-translate-medium-v2 to eu-west-1 completed by ivan at 2026-03-16T23:12:44Z :white_check_mark:
Ivan (Eng): Found the rollout policy: `fallback_policy=allow_compatible` and the canary health check had a 2s spike around 23:11 causing router to mark 1/3 nodes unhealthy — that triggered fallback to `rw-translate-base-en` during a short window. I'll revert the routing change for translation model family and force traffic to pinned canary while we validate.
Maria (CS): Customer is requesting immediate rollback for eu-west traffic or a targeted rule to avoid en-only fallback. They're impacted on live traffic (support ticket P0).
Suki (Support): Action items: 1) Ivan to apply temporary routing change (flip `fallback_policy` to `reject` for `translate` family in eu-west). 2) Jacob to validate that v2 binary itself doesn't produce language regressions with direct pinned inference. 3) Maria to get customer to share 5 more request IDs and output diffs. 4) Support to keep customer updated every 30m until resolved.
Ivan (Eng): Making the rollback now, ETA 8 minutes. I'll also check autoscaler logs — there might have been an allocation throttling event causing node unavailability.
Jacob (ML): Local test results: v2 binary produces Spanish output when run directly, no sign of tokenizer-induced English fallback. Suggests routing fallback is root cause. Also will run full regression suite on multilingual prompt set overnight and post results.
Maria (CS): Customer confirmed English output decreased after we temporarily reverted the routing policy. They're still seeing a few edge cases — sending extra request ids.
Suki (Support): Please attach the 5 new request ids here. Also let's schedule a postmortem for the rollout (include runbook gap: permissive fallback policy for mixed-locale models).
Ivan (Eng): Added ticket INF-4583 and assigned to eng-runtime, routing config diff at https://redwood.internal/routing/diffs/INF-4583.
Maria (CS): Thanks team — customer is on a 1:1 with support now and appreciates the quick revert. We'll keep monitoring and update when Jacob's regression run completes. :pray:
Jacob (ML): Will post regression results in #eng-ml tomorrow morning.
Suki (Support): Closing the escalation loop: we'll convert this thread to the PM postmortem once regression and routing fixes are in place. :white_check_mark:
